text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- News of Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's decision to seek hospital care for minor heart rhythm problem in Copenhagen on Tuesday came eight hours after Lipponen went to the hospital.
- An estimated one-third of Finnish farmers file faulty applications for European Union support thereby losing tens of thousands of markka in the process.
- Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari on trip to Estonia said he hopes Estonian-Russian talks on border dispute will reach a successful conclusion.
- Thousands of high school students now graduate in the autumn, breaking centuries old tradition of spring graduation.
- Finnish-made research instruments aboard Mars-bound Russian spacecraft to be launched at weekend.
- Finland could begin limiting road transport permits to foreigners if Russia does not stop demanding extra charges from Finnish truckers, transport ministry official says.
- Prospects for metal industry uncertain as order backlogs unusually low in comparison with last few years.
- Mining and metals group Outokumpu says Larox Oy has infringed its patent on filter equipment -- demands 20 million markka in lawsuit.
- Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto says Sweden's EMU report indicates that Sweden will join third stage of monetary union.
- Financial Supervision official says new register of corporate insiders helps authorities monitor insider trading.
- New Finnish representative to European Parliament Pertti Paasio likes Strasbourg legislature's practice of applauding good speeches -- says Finnish lawmakers should adopt it.
- Vice president of forestry group UPM-Kymmene says company has no plans to sell luxury yacht-builder Nautor, maker of the famous Swan sailboats.
